metadata.title: R4: Economic Inequality
metadata.description: Donor-favored policy concentrates wealth, widens inequality, fuels the belief that the system is unfair, drives anti-institution sentiment and polarization, increases campaign costs — and locks in dependence on big donors.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Policy Responsiveness to Donors
nodes.description: Degree to which legislation reflects donor preferences over the median voter.

nodes.label: Wealth Concentration
nodes.description: Share of national wealth held at the top — both cause and consequence of donor-favored policy.

nodes.label: Economic Inequality
nodes.description: The broader income and wealth gap — Gini coefficient, median wage stagnation, mobility.

nodes.label: Perception System Is Unfair
nodes.description: Citizens' sense that hard work no longer reliably leads to mobility and that institutions favor insiders.

nodes.label: Trust In Government
nodes.description: The percentage of citizens who say they trust the federal government to do what is right.

nodes.label: Anti-Institution Sentiment
nodes.description: Generalized hostility toward 'the establishment' — distinct from frustration with specific policies.

nodes.label: Political Polarization
nodes.description: Ideological and emotional distance between the parties — the same node that connects R2 and R4 in the full system.

nodes.label: Dependence on High-Dollar Campaigning
nodes.description: The reality that candidates without major donor support cannot afford to compete.

edges.description: Donor-favored policy concentrates wealth at the top.
Concentrated wealth widens the gap with everyone else.
Visible inequality fuels the belief that the rules favor insiders.
Believing the system is unfair drives trust in government down.
Low trust generalizes into hostility toward 'the establishment' as a whole.
Anti-establishment movements often align with — or get captured by — the polarized parties.
Polarized races are expensive — base mobilization, ad wars, opposition research all cost money.
Officials who depend on donors for re-election listen first to donors.

loops.label: R4: Economic Inequality
loops.description: Money in politics → unequal outcomes → unfair perception → distrust → polarization → more money needed.
